3) Private/VPC deployment details
- Number of environments: you called out prod + staging today; please confirm if you need a DR environment or additional dev clusters (we typically size per environment).
- Licensing model preference: per-environment license vs. fleet/license seat? Any procurement constraints we should know about.

4) Support & SLAs

Attachments: I’m attaching a rough pricing workbook template for you to fill with exact token counts and environment counts (FT-2026-042_rough_pricing.xlsx). I’ll also attach our private pricing template with common licensing options (redwood_private_pricing_template.pdf).

Next steps

- Token counts: The 1.2B is our best estimate for production + staging based on forecasted usage. That is billable tokens (we modeled at 1.2B). We will confirm exact breakdown but the split you listed (900M prod / 300M staging) is correct for planning.

- Budget: We're targeting a monthly spend in the $25k–$40k range to start for inference (can expand after proof-of-value). We understand that private deployments have different economics, but this is the budget band our finance leader has signaled.

- Target $/1M tokens: Ideally around $15–$30 per 1M tokens depending on support and environment requirements. If that’s unrealistic for private, share the closest options.

- Environments: We definitely need prod + staging, and a small DR environment (so 3 total). We may also want a dev sandbox but that could be shared for initial rollout — can you price both 3-env and 4-env options?

- Licensing: Procurement asked whether Redwood licenses per environment or there’s a fleet license. What do you recommend for flexibility + cost predictability? Also what is typical minimum commit (if any) for Private/VPC?

- Support: We expect Enterprise-tier support for the initial rollout (runbook integration + 24/7 paging).

If you can share an initial pricing table with the two environment variants and per-1M token unit economics under both Standard and Enterprise support, we can route to procurement.

Alex — thanks, this is perfect. Below is a short primer on our typical Private/VPC pricing and an initial set of scenarios that map to the inputs you provided. We’ll follow up with a filled workbook by tomorrow.

OPTIONAL LICENSE MODELS (typical)
- Per-environment license: fixed fee per environment (recommended when environments are strictly isolated and you need independent control planes).
- Fleet license: single license covering N environments (more predictable and often lower per-env cost for customers with multiple clusters).
- Hybrid: base fleet license + per-additional-env fee.

SUPPORT TIERS
- Standard: business hours, email & ticketing, 9×5 SLA
- Premium: extended hours, faster SLAs, 24/7 escalation on-call (no runbook integration)
- Enterprise: full 24/7 on-call, runbook & playbook integration, quarterly on-site/remote runbooks, and dedicated TAM. (This is what you requested.)

HIGH-LEVEL PRICING SCENARIOS (monthly) — ballpark, for modeling only
Inputs: 1.2B tokens / month (900M prod, 300M staging), 3 environments (prod, staging, DR)
- Scenario A (Per-env license, Enterprise support):
  • License: $18k / env / month x 3 envs = $54k
  • Inference unit economics (on-prem/private): $28 per 1M tokens (includes model runtime, ops, and patching) -> for 1.2B = $33,600
  • Total monthly (license + inference) = ~$87,600 (we can show commit vs. pay-as-you-go alternatives)

- Scenario B (Fleet license, Enterprise support, hybrid):
  • Fleet license (covers up to 4 envs): $40k / month
  • Inference unit economics with commit discounts: $20 per 1M tokens (with a 6–12 month committed monthly volume) -> for 1.2B = $24,000
  • Total monthly = ~$64,000

- Scenario C (Lower-touch Premium support):
  • Fleet license: $32k / month
  • Unit economics: $24 per 1M tokens -> $28,800
  • Total monthly = ~$60,800

Notes & levers
- Larger committed volumes drive unit economics down (we can model $/1M at 15, 20, 25 per 1M to show sensitivity).
- If you are willing to host smaller non-prod envs on a shared dev cluster, that lowers license count and significantly reduces total cost.
- We can structure minimum commit to align with your $25k–$40k target by recommending an initial free/discounted trial month + ramp commits.

Next steps
- I’ll populate the attached workbook with the two variants (3 envs vs 4 envs) and the three support options and send back a clear recommendation for procurement.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-min sizing call with Rishi (SE) to validate peak concurrency & latency SLOs — are you available Wed/Thu morning PST?

Sharing the attached pricing template now (redwood_private_pricing_template.pdf). I’ll also include an example commit proposal that aligns more closely to your $25k–$40k band if you prefer a low-risk entry path.

Thanks —
